summary: This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to establish a grant program that provides funding to owners and operators of eligible federally assisted multifamily housing, in partnership with qualified health care entities, to develop and implement programs promoting resident access to automated external defibrillators (AEDs) and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training and equipment.

scores.thoughts: This bill establishes a new grant program to promote access to AEDs and CPR in federally assisted multifamily housing, authorizing $25,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2031. This clearly represents an increase in government spending.

The primary purpose of this bill is to improve access to automated external defibrillators (AEDs) and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training in federally assisted housing, directly impacting emergency healthcare access and preparedness.

The bill targets federally assisted multifamily housing, which often serves low-income or vulnerable populations. By providing grants for AEDs and CPR in these settings, it enhances a safety net for residents in these specific housing types.

The bill authorizes $25 million annually for five years to fund a new grant program, directly increasing federal outlays and thereby accepting a modestly larger deficit to support the initiative. However, the legislation's core purpose is establishing the AED/CPR program rather than fiscal policy, so the deficit impact is real but peripheral.

The bill creates a federal grant program to expand access to AEDs and CPR training in federally assisted housing through government-funded equipment, training, and emergency planning, constituting direct government action to improve health preparedness and outcomes. This is the central purpose of the legislation.
